gaps.sentence: He stopped ___ coffee before bed and now sleeps much better.
gaps.explanation: 'Stop doing' = quit the activity; 'stop to drink' would mean pause in order to drink.

gaps.sentence: We managed ___ everyone before the storm hit.
The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: The children are looking forward to ___ Father Christmas.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: looking forward to meeting.

gaps.sentence: Don't forget ___ the plants while we're away.
gaps.explanation: forget + to-infinitive = fail to do something you should do.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford ___ another month abroad.
They're planning ___ the flat before selling it.
gaps.explanation: plan + to-infinitive (plan on + -ing also occurs informally): planning to redecorate.
bother + -ing (or to-infinitive): don't bother going. Both accepted.
